added_failures_note: measured: the reviewed manifest baseline_suite (revision ac67e760, base-gate.log, completed true, 349 passed, EXIT=0) and after_suite (revision a394f696, head-gate.log, completed true, 358 passed, EXIT=0) both record zero failures, so no failure was added.

0.reason: the asserts pin the shipped implement default the warning names; that figure moves only by a deliberate flight edit, which updates this test with it

1.reason: latent: no shipped, host or project flight declares a capability-class time_budget, so the class branch never names a key today

2.reason: accepted design: a refused node never launches, so its fence stops nothing, and the refusal's terminal output stays one document

3.reason: the case's guard is the preceding assertion that no fence line is emitted; the echo check is incidental

4.reason: the landing record states the thirteen cases the reviewed head ran, correcting the fragment's figure

findings.text: follow-on: the shipped implement default is written down as a literal in asserts at :195, :213 and :344, so the file turns red on the day reckon/schema/flight-defaults.yaml's roles.implement.time_budget moves — the very figure §52 was filed about, and a likely next change in this plan — while the docstring at :184 claims the figure is read rather than written down.

follow-on: the capability-class branch walks the classes in sorted order and keeps the last whose declared figure matches, but _effective_backend (reckon/crew/routing.py:182) applies only the node's own class and that class is never passed here, so with two classes declaring the same time_budget the alphabetically later one is named even when the node resolved at the earlier one — the mis-direction the function's own docstring says it exists to prevent.

follow-on: the fence line is withheld from both warnings and stderr when the dispatch refuses the node, a case §52's deliverable does not exempt; the withholding was forced by tests/test_crew.py's refusal-parity contract, which lies outside this node's write grant, and the worker disclosed the judgement in follow_ons for adjudication rather than deciding it silently.

follow-on: assert document["time_budget"] == "1h" compares the run's own echo of the budget against the value the test itself passed in, so it moves with its input and holds whatever the warning logic does; the guard in that case is the preceding assert not _fence_lines(document) at :252.

follow-on: the landed fragment's measure still reads "9 passed" for the node's test file, a figure three commits stale, while the file at the reviewed head carries thirteen cases, so the durable record of this node understates the gate the reviewed head actually ran.

item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is for a dispatch naming no --time-budget to warn, in its result and on stderr, when its resolved default fence is under a quarter of the node's own estimate or its named section's declared effort; reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1184 gates that emission and reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:427-455 builds the one line, appended to resolution.warnings and printed to stderr.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at the run directory; status complete, seven commits (1a7eef89, d5bbf4221, a394f6960, 72d00db8d, e35d69742, 4f762e145, 19a4cb53), tests line naming the new file's pytest command, baseline_suite and after_suite both carrying revision, command, exit_status, log_path, completed true and failure_count 0, and a follow_ons entry recording the refusal-case judgement and the fragment refresh this round did not make; the test_logs list omits negative-control-f64640be2c4.log, which is on disk.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_bare_dispatch_names_a_fence_far_below_its_effort.py:195-253 and dispatch_plan.py:449 carry assertions that redden under the recorded revert controls, but the once-per-run guard at tests/test_a_bare_dispatch_names_a_fence_far_below_its_effort.py:476 calls the helper directly rather than through a dispatch, and no case exercises the non-dry dispatch path.
justifications.evidence: the arm's target list matches every tests/ file referencing reckon.crew.dispatch_plan plus the worker-window check and both arms close with bare EXIT=0 lines, but the 358-passed after_suite receipt is at a394f696, three commits short of the reviewed head, and the log for the repair round carries no revision header.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1186 follows the module's own resolution.warnings.append idiom at reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:605 and :617, and every added symbol names its mechanism with no plan or ticket identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1184 with reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:449 delivers the section's quarter-of-the-estimate warning in warnings and on stderr, but withholds it on a dispatch that refuses the node, a case §52's deliverable does not exempt.
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:288 now reads a section's effort through the picker's own reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:107 rather than restating it, and parses durations with reckon/crew/node.py:821, so no capability the repository owns is forked.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff ac67e760..19a4cb53 is inside the manifest's declared write paths and nothing outside them is touched.
